_comment: T-pending — ignore files are DECLARED and AUDITED, not left to accumulate.
Owner instruction 2026-08-31: 'manage and audit all gitignore files and other ignore files
to own the management of it'. The instruction was earned three times in a single session:
`.turbo/` and `scratch/` were reported as an Obsidian-vs-Quartz divergence when the real
cause was that both are TRACKED despite matching .gitignore; `check_final*.txt` were 2,792
lines of build log tracked despite `check*.txt`; and `w0m-ext/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` turned
out to be a gitignored document, so an edit to it would never survive a clone.
The through-line is one failure mode: A RULE AND THE INDEX DISAGREE, AND NOTHING NOTICES.
git cannot un-track a committed file by adding a pattern later, so every rule added after
the fact is silently inert for what already exists. Measured 2026-08-31: 540 such files.
Scope is declared rather than discovered, because most ignore files in this estate are not
ours: 11 third-party repos under _ext/, 10 vendored MLX repos under w0m-mlx/ext/, orca under
_in/, and a dozen written by tools (.codegraph, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .pytest_cache,
husky, serena). Auditing those would be auditing other people's decisions.

governed._comment: w0m-authored ignore files. An ignore file inside a governed repo that is not listed here is DRIFT — add it, or record it under `generated`.

generated._comment: Written by a tool, not by us. Matched as PATH PREFIXES so a multi-segment one like `.husky/_` works -- an earlier segment-wise check silently failed on it and reported husky's own file as estate drift.

vendored._comment: Third-party trees. Their ignore files are their authors' decisions and are none of our business.

_comment: Every governed repo's root .gitignore must carry these. They are the ones whose absence
could cost something, not a style baseline -- so `dist/` and `.DS_Store` are deliberately
NOT here. Each names the pattern and why.
IMPORTANT: this is defence in DEPTH, not the only guard. All 7 repos run a pre-commit
secret scan (verified 2026-08-31 via core.hooksPath -- an earlier probe that looked only
at .husky/pre-commit reported 6 of 7 missing and was WRONG). A missing rule here is a
thinner net, not an open door, and it must be reported as such.

rules.why: The estate removed w0m-web/.env (86 plaintext keys) under T119 and forbids re-introducing one. A repo with no rule invites the file back.
Dependency tree; committing it has broken installs and dwarfs the repo.
Private keys and certificates. Only w0m-api carried this rule as of 2026-08-31.
Private key material. NO repo carried this rule as of 2026-08-31 -- the widest single gap found.

exempt.why: Rust + Python repo (Cargo, uv). It has no JS toolchain, so the rule would guard against nothing. `.env`, `*.pem` and `*.key` still apply and are still required.

_comment: Files that are tracked while an ignore rule matches them. Each needs a REASON, and the
reason has to say which side is right -- keep the file and fix the rule, or honour the
rule and untrack the file. An entry with no decision recorded is not accepted, it is
deferred, and the audit says so.

entries.why: Shared editor config committed on purpose; the rule ignores the rest of .vscode/. The rule is right and so is the exception.
A TEMPLATE, and the reason the rule is `.env.*` rather than `.env`. Keeping it tracked is the point; it carries no values. The rule is right and so is the exception.
Shared editor config committed on purpose, same decision as w0m-web's. The rule ignores the rest of .vscode/.
As w0m-api — shared editor config, deliberately tracked.

An EXAMPLE wearing the real name: its own first line reads 'Example overrides for Cloudflare Terraform... You can copy it to terraform.tfvars'. Inspected 2026-08-31 — it holds zone_name and one boolean, no credentials. Left tracked rather than renamed because terraform AUTO-LOADS terraform.tfvars, so renaming it changes behaviour rather than just tidying a name.

_comment: Measured 2026-08-31 and NOT yet decided. Listed so the number is visible rather than
discovered again; the audit reports them without failing, because deciding them is owner
work and a gate that blocks on an undecided question just gets switched off (T135 AC8).

entries.note: 502 tiny status/env txt files (~30 KB tracked; the 35 MB on disk is the UNTRACKED build/deploy logs, which the rule correctly excludes). Committed 2026-03-05 in b4556926; the ignore rule came later and is inert for them. Untrack, or drop the rule.
Turborepo cache, tracked despite `.turbo/`. Reported as an Obsidian/Quartz divergence before the real cause was found.
Tracked despite an explicit rule at .gitignore:90.

A tfstate BACKUP, tracked despite `*.tfstate.*.backup`. Scanned 2026-08-31: 24 KB, 11 resources, ZERO sensitive-looking keys — so this is debris rather than exposure. tfstate normally does carry secrets, which is why the rule exists; untracking is the likely answer.
Rule `.gitignore:54` names this ONE file, yet it is tracked — someone wrote a rule for it and committed it anyway. 2.6 KB SVG from 2025-12-23. One of the two must go.
A Playwright script (`require('playwright')`), matched by `trigger_*.js` — a rule that clearly targets exactly these. Not referenced by manifest.json, so it is a dev utility rather than shipped code.
